This is a technical physics question — diagnosing a discrepancy between observed and theoretical ultrasound resolution. The deciding factor is capability on reasoning-heavy STEM tasks.

Plover-235B is meaningfully stronger on the benchmarks that matter here: MMLU-Pro (81.2 vs 75.4), GPQA Diamond (64.1 vs 55.6, a large gap on graduate-level science reasoning), and Arena-Hard (90.6 vs 82.7). These margins are well outside run-to-run variance and point to better performance on a quantitative physics puzzle.

The task has no harm-adjacent, distasteful, or adversarial content, so neither model's preference profile is triggered — Willet's aversions and generative appetite are irrelevant here, and the query is warm and friendly, which suits both. With behavioral factors neutral, the choice comes down to raw reasoning capability, and Plover wins on that.
